results.title: Review: Code review on your own machine, with optional AI | Product Hunt
results.content:
Title: Review: Code review on your own machine, with optional AI | Product Hunt
# Review. ## Code review on your own machine, with optional AI. A desktop app for Git branches and GitHub pull requests. Comment on any line, publish when you're ready, and add an AI reviewer with your own model, or none. Launch tags:Open Source•Developer Tools•Artificial Intelligence. I'm Hamed, and I made Review. I'm a developer and team lead. Since AI started writing so much of our code, reviewing it all has become the hardest part of my job. So I built Review: a desktop app for reviewing pull requests, where you can set up a team of AI reviewers from different providers to take the first pass. You still decide what gets published. - Opens your local Git branches and GitHub pull requests in one window. ⌘P jumps to any of them. - Pins each review to exact commits, so the diff doesn't shift when someone pushes. - Keeps your comments on your machine until you publish them to GitHub as a review. - Adds an AI reviewer if you want one: OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, OpenRouter, or a local model in Ollama or LM Studio. Your keys are stored in the system keychain. **What's different about the AI part**: it checks every change against a fixed set of rules (bugs, security, error handling, tests and more), and it shows which rules it actually checked, not just what it found. If a request fails, you can retry only the rules it missed. It can also call your MCP servers for context the code doesn't have, like the ticket behind a change. It's free, open source (MIT) and needs no account. It runs on macOS, Windows and Linux. One heads-up: the installers aren't signed yet, so your system will ask once the first time you open it. The website has the two-click fix. I'd love to know: what's the most annoying part of code review for you today? And which model would you plug in first? results.content:
Title: Vibinex Code-Review: A distributed process for reviewing pull requests. | Product Hunt
# Vibinex Code-Review. ## A distributed process for reviewing pull requests. If your team misses delivery deadlines due to rework or resolved issues reappear in your product, then this is the tool for you. Vibinex automatically distributes the review process among developers at a code-hunk level for better quality and faster delivery. No reviews yetBe the first to leave a review for Vibinex Code-Review. Across several companies, the most frustrating yet critical part of leading a project was setting up the code review process and getting it adopted. The core feature of Vibinex is the automatic distribution and assignment of code reviewing using git history. 2. Partially review a PR: You don't need to review every diff in a PR, just the code-hunks that are relevant to you. With Vibinex, you don't have to worry about miscommunication. Our open-source Rust program (Code: https://github.com/Alokit-Innova...) runs in your CI pipeline, parses your git history to extract only the relevant metadata (making it impossible to reproduce your code from it), and then SHA-encrypts every word in it, including your email aliases, making them unreadable, and only sends that to our servers. COMPATIBILITY: Code hosting: Github and Bitbucket Browsers: Chromium-based (Google Chrome, Microsoft Edge, Brave etc.) Note: If your team uses a different code-hosting service or web browser and is keen on using our tool, we'd be happy to build the integrations to get you started. 😍 How do you ensure that the code review assignments are distributed fairly and evenly among team members? Regarding the ongoing training, we are actually contemplating several ideas for using pull requests and the code itself to minimize the number of "knowledge transfer" meetings that tech team leaders have to conduct. I'd love to discuss this in more detail with you if you are open to it. I love the idea of continuous code reviewing, and being able to partially review a PR is a game-changer for time management ⏰. We plan to fix that this week so that it is much easier to get started with our product for any new developer.
